newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: AIB sees further progress in second half.
newsitem.headline: AIB sees further progress in second half.

text.p: Allied Irish Banks Plc said on Thursday said the outlook in its principal markets remained positive and it expected to make further progress in the second half of the year.

The bank, which reported a 20 percent rise in pre-tax profit for the half-year to June 30 to 242.2 million punts, said the strong profit growth was delivered by better performances from all its divisions.
AIB said in a statement that good demand for its products and services in the Republic of Ireland, Northern Ireland and Britain was one of the key factors behind the increase.

The bank also attributed the rise in profits to growth in retail and commercial lending in the U.S. and a large rise in fee income and to a substantially increased contribution from its capital markets division, particularly Treasury operations.
AIB's new Polish subsidiary, Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) made a profit contribution of 12.3 million punts after funding.
Profits in AIB Bank, the retail division, rose to 130 million in the first six months of 1997, an increase of 24 percent.

The bank said the strong performance was due to a number of factors including higher levels of branch lending, with demand particularly strong in the Republic of Ireland, reflecting a buoyant economy.
AIB's U.S. operations reported an 11 percent rise in profits to 62.9 million while profits in the capital markets division rose by 33 percent to 42.6 million.

The bank said key factors behind the rise were a rise in Treasury income and good growth in investment banking, particularly from Goodbody Stockbrokers which achieved a substantially higher contribution in the half-year period.
It also enjoyed strong loan and deposit growth in corporate banking.
